rv.q: But, for all the efforts of the director and cast, it made me want to see two later, darker plays that knowingly used Gogol: JB Priestley’s An Inspector Calls and Dario Fo’s Accidental Death of an Anarchist.
Tom Rosenthal stars in a well-oiled production of Nikolai Gogol’s classic Russian-Ukrainian satire at Chichester Festival Theatre
It’s a frustrating glimpse into something more substantial that is never fully realised, however.
All in all, the show feels too long and slow to work as a farcical, quick-fire, socio-political comedy.
It is perfect territory for a satirical comedy and yet the production is strangely unfunny and laboured.
As an ensemble piece, true to Gogol and in period, this could hardly be bettered.

cn.t: Gogol's satire receives a mixed reception, with critics divided on Gregory Doran's farcical approach. While some praise its comic energy and topical resonance, others feel the production leans too heavily into farce at the expense of sharper satire.
